criteria.evidence:
FAILING CLAUSE 1 - permanent local/external divergence. (a) Occurrence overrides never push. `grep -rn 'insert(calendarProviderSyncQueue)' src/ --include='*.ts' | grep -v spec` returns exactly five sites: /Users/tarunchintakunta/Personal/streamline/streamlineos-backend/src/modules/calendar/calendar.service.ts:193 (create), :315 (update), :442 (delete), calendar-provider-sync-sweep.service.ts:177 (the compensating delete) and calendar-provider-webhook.service.ts:184 (the drift requeue). None is in calendar-recurrence.service.ts. Read directly: `upsertOccurrenceException` (calendar-recurrence.service.ts:105-155) and `cancelOccurrence` (:157+) write calendar_event_exceptions, dead-letter the reminder outbox rows, and call `bumpSeries` (:94-102, `localVersion: sql\`localVersion + 1\`` + updatedAt) -- and enqueue nothing. So moving one instance of a synced weekly series changes it locally and never in Google. (b) Recurrence is never transmitted at all. /Users/tarunchintakunta/Personal/streamline/streamlineos-backend/src/modules/calendar/external-calendar-sync.service.ts:8-16 `interface PushEventInput { title; description; startIso; endIso; allDay; attendeeEmails; addConference }` -- there is no rrule/recurrence field, and `grep -n 'rrule|recurrence' external-calendar-sync.service.ts` returns nothing. The sweep's update branch (calendar-provider-sync-sweep.service.ts:198-206) pushes only title/description/startIso/endIso. A recurring series therefore reaches the provider as ONE event, permanently.

FAILING CLAUSE 2 - monotonic version ordering for deletes. calendar.service.ts:441-449 enqueues the delete with `{ orgId, eventId, connectionId, operation: 'delete', externalEventId, payload }` and NO `eventLocalVersion`, while the create (:193-199) and update (:315-322) both stamp it. A delete is therefore unordered against the version chain the same queue uses to supersede stale updates.
